titles: Fake FBI Calls Hit Scam Victims in 2026
Scammed? Why the 2nd Call Is Worse 🚨
The 2nd Scam Call Costs More 🚨
Who's Really Calling From the FBI? 📞
Scammed Twice by the Same Gang? 🚨
s032.description:
Fake FBI "recovery" calls: why scam victims get scammed a second time.
How the IC3 impersonation / fund-recovery scam works, and the one rule that stops it.

After a scam, a second call comes: someone posing as the FBI or its Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) says they can get your money back for a small upfront fee. The FTC warns that recovery scammers buy lists of people who've already been scammed. The FBI (PSA, July 2026) warns of AI deepfake videos of an FBI leader sending victims to a spoofed IC3 site. The real IC3 never contacts you first and never asks for payment to recover lost funds.

Sources:
https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2026/PSA260720
https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2026/08/have-you-lost-money-scam-watch-scammers-who-say-they-can-help
https://www.avasc.org/briefings/election-week-scam-surge-fake-ftc-agents-fake-ic3-recovery-fake-ballots-2026-11-02

titles: Who Bought All the RAM in 2026? 🧠
Why Phones Got Pricier in 2026 📱
RAM Up 80% in One Quarter. Why? 📈
Your Phone Is Paying for ChatGPT? 📱
Who's Eating All the Memory? 🧠
s033.description:
Why are phones and laptops getting more expensive in 2026? The AI memory shortage, explained.
RAM (DRAM) prices are surging as AI data centres buy up memory.

TrendForce says DRAM contract prices rose about 80% in Q2 2026 and about 40% in Q3, with roughly 20% more forecast for Q4 — about three times the start-of-year level if that holds. AI data centres pay more for memory than phone and PC makers, so chipmakers shift capacity to AI memory and less is left for consumer devices. Simplified: "tripled" is a cumulative estimate based on a forecast.

Sources:
https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/10/20/news-dram-prices-seen-rising-20-qoq-in-4q26-despite-slower-gains-ai-demand-tight-supply-support-outlook/
https://www.theregister.com/2026/02/02/dram_prices_expected_to_double/

Scenes are AI-generated illustrations.
#Shorts #RAM #AI
s033.comment: Would you pay more for AI in your phone? 👇 TrendForce: DRAM contract prices +~80% in Q2 2026, +~40% in Q3, ~+20% forecast for Q4.

titles: Someone Bought the Eiffel Tower? 🗼
Who Sold the Eiffel Tower? 🗼
The Man Who Sold the Eiffel Tower 🗼
Why Didn't the Buyer Call Police? 🗼
The Eiffel Tower Scam Nobody Reported
s034.description:
The man who sold the Eiffel Tower: Victor Lustig's 1925 con, explained.
How a fake government letterhead and a luxury hotel fooled a Paris scrap dealer.

The Eiffel Tower was built on a 20-year permit. In 1925, con man Victor Lustig posed as a government official, invited scrap-metal dealers to the Hôtel de Crillon and said the state would secretly sell the tower for scrap. Dealer André Poisson paid, plus a bribe, and Lustig vanished. Poisson was too embarrassed to go to the police, so Lustig tried the same con again — this time a dealer called the police and he fled. Parts of the story come from later retellings.

Sources:
https://www.toureiffel.paris/en/news/130-years/how-did-radio-save-tower
https://thehustle.co/originals/the-con-man-who-sold-the-eiffel-tower-twice-1
https://www.mentalfloss.com/crime/smooth-operator-how-victor-lustig-sold-eiffel-tower

Scenes are AI-generated illustrations.
#Shorts #history #scam

titles: De Beers' $6.8B Problem 💎
The 4 Words That Sold Diamonds 💎
The 1947 Slogan Behind Your Ring 💎
Why You Can't Resell Your Diamond 💎
Your Ring Was a Marketing Trick? 💎
s035.description:
"A Diamond Is Forever": how De Beers made diamonds feel rare, and why lab-grown diamonds are breaking the spell.
Why diamonds resell for so little, explained.

De Beers once controlled most of the world's diamond supply. In 1947 its ad agency, N.W. Ayer, wrote "A Diamond Is Forever" — and "forever" discouraged resale, so few people learned how little a used diamond fetches. Later ads pushed "two months' salary"; the share of US brides with a diamond ring rose from about 10% to about 80% (Al Jazeera). Lab-grown stones now cost up to 80–90% less, and Anglo American has written De Beers down by $6.8 billion since 2023.

Sources:
https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2025/9/14/how-the-diamond-engagement-ring-was-invented-and-sold-around-the-world
https://europeanbusinessmagazine.com/de-beers-diamond-collapse/

Scenes are AI-generated illustrations.
#Shorts #diamonds #DeBeers
s035.comment: Mined or lab-grown, which would you buy? 👇 Anglo American's De Beers writedowns: $1.6B (2023) + $2.9B (2024) + $2.3B (2025) = $6.8B.

titles: The Coin That Trapped Coca-Cola 🥤
Why Coke Asked for a 7½¢ Coin 🥤
Why a Coke Cost a Nickel Forever 🥤
The Price Coke Couldn't Change 🥤
Eisenhower Said No to Coca-Cola? 🥤
s036.description:
Why did a Coke cost 5 cents for 70 years? The nickel Coke, explained.
How a 1899 bottling deal and nickel-only vending machines froze Coca-Cola's price.

In 1899 two lawyers got Coke's bottling rights with the syrup price fixed permanently. Coke tied its brand to five cents, and its vending machines took a single nickel — the next coin up, a dime, would have doubled the price. Coca-Cola asked the US Treasury for a 7.5-cent coin, and its boss even raised it with his hunting buddy, President Eisenhower. The answer was no. Inflation won, and the nickel Coke was gone by 1959.

Sources:
https://www.npr.org/sections/money/2012/11/15/165143816/why-coke-cost-a-nickel-for-70-years
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fixed_price_of_Coca-Cola_from_1886_to_1959

Scenes are AI-generated illustrations.
#Shorts #history #inflation
s036.comment: What price do you wish never changed? 👇 NPR: Coca-Cola asked the US Treasury for a 7.5-cent coin. It never happened.
